Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
1013 AM EDT Sun Oct 18 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
The growing season has ended west of the Blue Ridge Mountains.
The need for Frost Advisories tonight in the piedmont will be 
determined by early afternoon.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Below normal temperatures with frost and freeze
  concerns continue through Monday morning.
 
- 2) Potential for isolated showers and breezy conditions next
  week as a Nor'easter lurks offshore.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Below normal temperatures with frost and freeze
concerns continue through Monday morning.

Surface high pressure settles over the Mid-Atlantic today
through Monday with below normal temperatures expected. High 
temperatures today rise into the 50s to low 60s across the 
forecast area with overnight lows tonight dropping into the 30s 
to mid 40s. Additional Frost Advisories will likely be needed 
for Monday morning where the growing season continues east of
the Blue Ridge. Some pockets could fall below freezing, but will
need to evaluate incoming guidance to determine if this will
occur on a widespread enough basis to need a Freeze Warning.

Temperatures will climb slightly Monday and Monday night, with 
additional Frost Advisories appearing unlikely.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Potential for isolated showers and breezy 
conditions next week as a Nor'easter lurks offshore.

Particularly for locations along or east of I-95, a developing 
Nor'easter off of the Mid-Atlantic coast guides weather conditions 
late next week. East of I-95, scattered shower potential, wind 
strength, and coastal flood risk are dependent on the track of this 
system. Regardless of where this Nor-easter tracks, locations 
further inland, particularly west of the Blue Ridge and Catoctin 
mountain ranges, are expected to remain dry in part due to 
downsloping west of these mountain ranges. Daily daytime 
temperatures are expected to remain fairly consistent throughout 
this time period reaching into mid to upper 60s (50s at higher 
elevations). Cooler than average overnight temperatures on Monday 
persist through the end of the week.

An omega block setup and a predominantly zonal flow next week 
generally leads to uncertain but weaker systems. Current guidance 
continues to exhibit moderate spread when it comes to the placement 
of the low and timing as it meanders along the coast. On Monday, a 
developing low pressure system is located off the North Carolina 
coast. During the middle of next week, this Nor'easter crawls 
northward, remaining off the Mid-Atlantic coast. Guidance differs 
most at towards the end of the week and into the weekend. Most 
solutions keep this Nor'easter well off shore, maintaining dry 
conditions throughout our region. Some guidance meanders the low 
toward the coast Thursday and Friday, increasing the potential for 
isolated showers and breezier conditions exclusively along and east 
of the I-95 corridor. As for any marine and coastal flooding 
concerns, see the corresponding discussions below.

&&

.AVIATION /14Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
North/northeasterly winds are expected today and Monday, 
gusting around 15 knots each afternoon. Winds shift to
northwesterly on Tuesday, gusting 15 to 20 knots in the
afternoon. VFR conditions are expected each day with surface
high pressure yielding dry conditions. 

Tuesday through Saturday, primarily VFR conditions are expected 
amongst all terminals with periods of sub-VFR mainly to the east, 
potentially including BWI, DCA, and MTN. A few showers are possible 
on the east side of the ZDC airspace with the Nor'easter lurking 
offshore. Winds will generally be out of the northeast at 10 to 20 
kts with gusts up to 30 kts, especially near the waters.

&&

.MARINE...
Small Craft Advisory conditions continue today, though gradually
contracting toward southern Maryland, with northwest winds 
gusting around 20 knots. Elevated winds continue through early 
next week as a Nor'easter develops off the Carolina coast with 
SCA criteria winds possible. 

Through Thursday, a developing Nor'easter off the Mid- Atlantic
coast delivers a prolonged period of SCA conditions. Over the 
wider, central Chesapeake Bay, gale condtions are a possibility 
this period. Confidence is currently low for gales based upon 
the track of the system with projected winds out of the 
northeast at 10- 20 kts with gusts up to 30 kts at times.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Tides are snapping back today as northerly winds slacken. A 
developing Nor'easter off the Mid-Atlantic coast will lead to 
tidal anomalies continuing to rise into the upcoming week. 
Sensitive locations (i.e. Annapolis) will have a chance to reach
minor flooding thresholds during the high tide cycle tonight, 
and again during the middle of next week. Considerable 
uncertainty remains on how exactly this Nor'easter will track 
and subsequently affect the tide levels.

&&
